Answer: A
Reason: Figure 3 demonstrates extensive, diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates (a "white-out" appearance) with a normal-sized cardiac silhouette, which is the classic radiographic presentation of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) rather than cardiogenic pulmonary edema. The progression from patchy opacities to this severe bilateral involvement aligns with the non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema characteristic of ARDS.
